question: How many named storms will there be in the 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season?

calls.reasoning: NHC record shows 9 named storms (Arthur through Isaias); NHC's 13 Oct 2pm outlook expects no formation for 7 days, so only ~20 Oct-30 Nov remains. Strong El Nino shear (NOAA Aug outlook 7-13 NS) suppresses late-season genesis; El Nino analog years (1997, 2002, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2023, counted from memory) averaged ~0.7 storms after mid-October vs ~1.5 climatologically. Estimated additional storms: P(0)~45%, P(1)~33%, P(2)~15%, P(3+)~7%. Markets: Polymarket only prices hurricane counts (1-3 hurricanes at 0.98), a near-miss contract that confirms a quiet season; no named-storm market found.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia 2026 Atlantic season page (fetched 2026-10-13): 9 named storms, all listed by name: Arthur (Jun 17), Bertha (Jul 19), Cristobal (Aug 12), Dolly (Aug 27), Edouard (Aug 31), Fay (Sep 19), Gonzalo (Sep 25), Hanna (Sep 28), Isaias (Oct 6, hurricane Oct 8, landfall FL Panhandle Oct 11). No unnamed depressions listed. Next name: Josephine.
- The Hill timeline (2026-10-12) says 'ten named systems', but its own list contains only nine; the Orlando Sentinel (2026-10-12) says nine. Treat the count as 9.
- NHC Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook, 2026-10-13 2pm EDT: 'Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days'; no areas of interest. The Cape Verde system NHC gave 20% on Oct 12 has dropped out of the outlook (upper winds became hostile).
- NOAA August update: 7-13 named storms, 2-6 hurricanes, 0-2 major, citing an extremely strong El Nino producing shear. Isaias became the first hurricane on Oct 8, near the record-late first hurricane (Oct 8, 1905).
- Status quo: the count stays at 9 unless a new storm forms between about Oct 20 and Nov 30.
- Base rates: across 1991-2020 (all seasons), roughly 1.5 named storms form after Oct 13 on average. Across El Nino seasons (1997, 2002, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2023; approximate, from memory), roughly 0-1 storms formed after mid-October each, mean ~0.7: 1997 Grace (Oct 16); 2002 none; 2006 none; 2009 Ida (Nov); 2015 Kate (Nov); 2023 Tammy (Oct 18) plus possibly 1 more.
- Resolution: off the NHC count of named storms (including subtropical storms) for the 2026 season. Post-season reanalysis would come after Dec 1.
- Event window: Jun 1 -> Nov 30, 2026 per the fine print; as of 2026-10-13 ~74% elapsed (~48 days left, of which the next 7 have zero expected formation).
- Markets: Polymarket prices only hurricane counts, no named-storm contract found.
- Searched for but not found: a CSU/TSR late-season named-storm update, or a medium-range MJO/Caribbean genesis outlook for late October.
calls.reference_class: Named storms forming after ~Oct 13 in El Nino Atlantic seasons (1997, 2002, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2023), added to the current count of 9

calls.reasoning: Count is 9 as of Oct 13 (Arthur-Isaias, verified on Wikipedia and in news). The NHC 7-day outlook shows no Atlantic formation expected; the Cape Verde low is now ~0%. A strong, still-strengthening El Nino is driving high shear. In El Nino/quiet seasons, storms forming after mid-October numbered 0-1, occasionally 2. P(+0)~0.38, P(+1)~0.37, P(+2)~0.17, P(+3+)~0.08. No named-storm market found. Polymarket's hurricane-count contracts (1-3 hurricanes at 0.98) are a near-miss contract and consistent with a quiet season.
calls.dossier:
- Named storms so far in 2026 (Wikipedia, checked 2026-10-13): 9 — Arthur Jun 17, Bertha Jul 19, Cristobal Aug 12, Dolly Aug 27, Edouard Aug 31, Fay Sep 19, Gonzalo Sep 25, Hanna Sep 28, Isaias Oct 6 (hurricane Oct 8, Cat 2 landfall near Destin FL Oct 11). One hurricane total. Next name: Josephine.
- The Hill (2026-10-12) said 'ten named systems', but its list contains nine; Wikipedia and the Orlando Sentinel both say nine.
- NHC outlook (2026-10-13): no Atlantic tropical cyclones; formation not expected in the next 7 days. The low west-northwest of Cabo Verde is in strong upper-level winds, with 48h and 7-day formation chances near 0% (an Oct 12 Orlando Sentinel report had it at 20%).
- CPC ENSO (Oct 2026): strong El Nino still strengthening, likely strong-to-very-strong through Jan-Mar 2027. This raises Atlantic shear.
- NOAA August update: 7-13 named storms, 2-6 hurricanes; average season 14 named storms.
- Status quo: the count stays at 9 unless a new storm forms by Nov 30.
- Base rates (approximate, from memory of HURDAT): named storms forming after mid-October, over El Nino / quiet seasons: 1982 0, 1997 1 (Grace), 2002 0, 2006 0, 2009 1 (Ida), 2015 1 (Kate), 2018 1 (Oscar), 2023 ~1 (Tammy). Over all seasons 1991-2020 the average is about 1.5-2 per season after mid-October.
- Upside mechanisms: late-season Caribbean/Gulf genesis (Central American gyre); subtropical storms in the subtropical Atlantic in November, which happen even in El Nino years.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the NHC count of named storms (including subtropical) for the 2026 season. A post-season reanalysis could add an unnamed storm, but this is rare and may come after resolution.
- Event window: Jun 1, 2026 -> Nov 30, 2026 per the fine print; as of 2026-10-13, about 61% elapsed. The next 7 days are effectively closed per the NHC outlook.
- Markets: no named-storm count market found. Polymarket hurricane-count markets exist (a different quantity).
- Searched but could not find: CSU/NOAA October-specific late-season outlooks; the MJO phase forecast for late October-November.

- Season context: extremely strong El Nino, high shear. NOAA August update: 7-13 named storms. ACE about 18 as of Oct 10 (Wikipedia). Isaias tied the 1905 record for latest first hurricane.

Strong El Nino years, recalled from memory and not checked: 1997 had none after Oct 20, 2023 none, 2015 one (Kate, Nov 9), 2009 one (Ida, Nov 4), 1982 none. Conditional mean about 0.4-0.6.

calls.reasoning: NHC count stands at 9 named storms (Arthur–Isaias) as of Oct 13; NHC expects no formation for 7 days, so the live window is ~Oct 20–Nov 30. Strong, strengthening El Niño shear suppresses late genesis; El Niño analog years (1982, 1997, 2002, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2023) averaged ~0.5–0.6 storms after mid-October versus ~1.5 climatologically. Model additions as Poisson ~0.6: ~55% stays at 9, ~33% reaches 10, ~12% reaches 11+. No named-storm market exists; Polymarket hurricane-count contracts (1–3 at 0.98) only confirm a quiet season.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual base: 9 named storms, a 7-day no-formation outlook from NHC, and a strong El Niño; The Hill's figure of 'ten' contradicts its own list and was discarded. The only real dispute is a judgment call on the expected number of late-season additions (runs implied about 0.6 to 0.9). I checked the El Niño analog years against my own recall of HURDAT (0,1,0,0,1,1,1 from about Oct 13, mean ~0.57). The window effectively starts Oct 20, which lowers that slightly, while November subtropical storms raise it slightly, so I chose λ≈0.62, closest to Run 3, with a slightly fatter right tail. No web access on this run.
